column1: # GRADUATED 2026-08-28 — this file is empty by design.
# The eight `is <predicate-type>` rows it carried now live in
# lang/spec/fnpred.tsv §7, beside the typed-def forms they mirror — which is
# exactly where this file's own graduation note said they would go.
# The note's DIAGNOSIS was wrong in a way worth keeping. It read:
#   "A predicate type's constraint IS a function value, so asking `4 is Even`
#    walks that value into `is` and hits the Stage 3 compile failure."
# A predicate NODE is not a function value walking anywhere. It is a bare
# type literal that rides as data; the body runs through the callback seam
# (RunPredicate -> InvokeCallbackFn), never the tape, so the re-step the
# compile failure defends against was never in play. What DID block the graduation
# was invisible from here: the callback seam's nested arm declined every
# detached unit, so the body interpreted inside the handler and admitting the
# rows would have hidden an island rather than removed one. Once foreign
# units became hostable mid-run (eng/go/vm_foreign_unit.go) the rows compiled
# with no interpreter entry at all.
# Two shapes the file never carried graduated with them — the input-type gate
# (`"x" is Even`) and the type literal itself (`Even is Even`).
# Kept as a stub rather than deleted: the frontier ledger is a census, and a
# file that vanishes reads as a file nobody measured.
